**Thesis.** The six loss-making solar projects are nearly finished, so 2026 is the trough, but full recovery to 2025's ~5.4% operating margin takes until 2029 because renewables volume is shrinking, and higher interest and amortization keep EPS a year behind; on that path adjusted EPS reaches ~$5.90 and the stock is worth ~$77 at 13x, about 2% a year from $71.

**Variant view.** The Street's FY2027 rebound is about a year early: Q3 Energy revenue fell 17.6% even with PayneCrest, management describes solar new work as slow to start in every 2026 release, the Q4 guide implies only $0.59-0.74 of adjusted EPS, and Q3 interest annualizes near $57M; this call has FY2027 adjusted EPS of $4.59 against the Street's $5.32 and reaches the Street's number only in FY2028, so the stock is fair rather than cheap.

**Catalysts.**

- Q4 2026 results and first FY2027 outlook (Around February 22, 2027 (estimated from the February 23, 2026 release))
- Q1 2027 results (Early May 2027)
- Permanent COO appointment (Open)
- Pace of utility-scale solar new starts (2027)

**Pre-mortem** (written at decision time).

- Solar volume keeps falling and the Energy cost base is not resized, so Energy margin sits at 5-6% through 2027. — watch: Q1 2027 Energy gross margin below 7% and a FY2027 revenue guide below 5% growth
- Claims on the six projects settle below their carrying value, or a new fixed-price gas or data-center project overruns. — watch: Any new loss provision or contract-asset write-down in a 10-Q or release after Q3 2026
- Working capital does not unwind, operating cash stays weak, leverage rises and buybacks stop. — watch: FY2026 operating cash flow below $100M; net debt above 2.5x trailing adjusted EBITDA
- Further leadership turnover leaves the recovery without an execution team. — watch: CFO or segment-president departure on an 8-K Item 5.02 in 2027
- Utilities margins revert as storm work and favorable closeouts fade, removing the steady half's offset. — watch: Utilities gross margin below 10% for two consecutive quarters

**Kill criteria.**

- Initial FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint below $4.00 (check by 2027-03-15) — open
- A new loss provision or guidance cut tied to renewables project overruns disclosed after the Q3 2026 release (check by 2027-05-31) — open
- Net debt above 2.5x trailing adjusted EBITDA at any 2027 quarter end (check by 2027-11-15) — open

**Probability claims.**

- 75%: FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS, reported with Q4 2026 results, is between $2.10 and $2.25 inclusive. (resolves by 2027-03-15)
- 30%: Primoris issues initial FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance with a midpoint of at least $5.00 by March 15, 2027. (resolves by 2027-03-15)
- 70%: Total backlog reported at December 31, 2026 is at least $13.5 billion. (resolves by 2027-03-15)
- 60%: Q4 2026 Energy segment gross margin, as reported in the Q4 release segment table, is at least 7.0%. (resolves by 2027-03-15)
- 55%: FY2026 net cash provided by operating activities is at least $150 million. (resolves by 2027-03-15)

**What would change the view.**

- More bullish: FY2027 adjusted EPS guide at or above $5.00 with revenue growth guided above 8%
- More bullish: Energy gross margin at or above 8% in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027 with no new loss provisions
- More bullish: the same evidence at a price in the low $60s
- More bearish: FY2027 adjusted EPS guide below $4.00, or any further renewables loss provision
- More bearish: FY2026 operating cash flow below $100 million

**Independent review: grade B** (evidence 4, valuation 3, variant view 4, risk 4, calibration 4). Counter-case: On the call's own numbers this is an Avoid, not a Watch. The base case needs GAAP operating margin back to about 5.3% before amortization, a level the report admits was reached only in 2024–2025, and a 16.6x GAAP exit multiple above every 2018–2023 year-end (8.9–14.3x); at that range's 12.8x median, base FY2029 GAAP EPS of $5.16 is worth about $66, below $71.24. Meanwhile nine-month operating cash flow was $8.9M, the balance sheet went from $65.6M of net cash to $580.8M of net debt, Q3 interest of $14.3M is running near $57M a year against the $38–45M modeled, and the board has just authorized $250M more of buybacks. Put 30% on a -48% bear and the honest expected return is near zero.

**Response.** Accepted most of it. Changes: interest re-based on the Q3 run-rate (base $52M/$48M/$44M, bear $58-60M, bull $50M/$45M/$40M); add-backs now taxed at each case's effective rate, matching Schedule 3 ($24.6M on $73.7M); FY2026 revenue base lowered from the $7.07B consensus to $7.00B because the Q4 guide implies a weak quarter; base exit multiple cut from 14x to 13x adjusted (15.3x GAAP); variant view corrected from 'two years early' to 'about a year early'; factual fixes to the Energy margin vs target range, PayneCrest backlog date, MSA backlog wording and the bear multiple's place in the historical range. Fair value fell from $81.23 to $75.40 (+1.9% a year), base from $85.53 to $76.96, bear to $34.26, bull to $133.20. The report now states that at the old 12.8x GAAP median the base is worth about $64. Not changed: the stance stays Watch because the rule gives Watch at +1.9% a year, and the base keeps a multiple one point above the 2018-2023 range because Utilities MSA work (backlog +27% this year) is a larger share of the mix than in the pipeline years; no peer multiples were captured to test that. The weights stay 30/50/20: the counter-case's near-zero return is close to what the revised numbers say, and it is inside the Watch band rather than below it.

**Data notes.** Price is the November 9, 2026 committed close; PRIM closed at $69.88 on November 10 (StockAnalysis), not yet in data/prices. Adjusted EPS is company-defined non-GAAP (adds back stock compensation, intangible amortization, transaction and severance costs); scenario multiples are also given on GAAP EPS in the report. No peer multiples, call transcript, or investor presentation were captured; web search was unavailable during this run. Revised after independent review (grade B): FY2026 revenue base, interest, add-back tax rate and base exit multiple changed; fair value fell from $81.23 to $75.40. See review.
